about: Workflows every copy of scripts/check-policies.mjs in the fleet has to judge the same way.
Each row is one workflow file (workflow, one string per line) and the run-expression violations the checker must report for it:
violations lists every { line, expression } that checkWorkflows reports as an expression in a run script, and nothing else. An empty list means the workflow must pass.
One row per fixed bypass: a fix to any copy of the checker adds a row here, so every copy without the fix fails its tests.
The canonical copy lives in Danathar/dns-failover (policies/check-policies-corpus.json). Change it there first, then copy it byte for byte; each other copy pins its SHA-256.

rows.why: a space and # before the expression is not a YAML comment inside a run scalar, and GitHub still substitutes the issue title into the command
a # inside a double-quoted run scalar is part of the string, so the expression after it still reaches the shell
every line of a run: | block is script text, so a # in it hides nothing from GitHub's substitution
the safe spellings stay allowed once # is no longer stripped: the title passed through env:, and the issue number, which is not attacker text
